correctness.rationale: Exact finite incidence proof: each factor is evaluated at all starts and lengths; a candidate is an attractor iff it hits every factor-position mask. Inclusion-minimal masks are equivalent constraints. Every size-three candidate on T_k for k>=2 uses one position of each alphabet letter, and the exhaustive two-letter-pair/remaining-third-bit intersection enumerates every such candidate. The certificate contains every surviving triple for 0<=k<=11 and was independently recomputed. A separate factor-by-position incidence algorithm reproduced the complete collections through k=9. This proves the exact finite scope but no infinite recurrence.

value.rationale: The exact number and complete locations of all smallest attractors distinguish morphic families with the same minimum size, precisely the gap motivated in 2026 by Banbara et al. This is the canonical ternary episturmian example. Eleven nontrivial natural substitution levels up to length 927 supply a complete structural finite census, with non-obvious transitions (224->416 rather than 448) useful as stringent tests of any future all-order formula. The target is a natural invariant, not an arbitrary numerical statistic. No paper-sized all-order theorem or downstream application is asserted.
